about.label: 01 / ABOUT
about.paragraph1: My career brings together technology, management, and experience in environments where systems need to work in the real world. Over the years, I have built solutions to simplify processes, automate workflows, and turn operational challenges into practical digital products.
about.paragraph2: Today, my work focuses on software development, artificial intelligence, automation, and digital transformation — always pursuing solutions that deliver measurable impact and make sense for the people who actually use them.

case.seoTitle: Hefesto | Technology for Emergency Operations | Marcelo Pires de Farias
case.seoDescription: Case study of Hefesto, a platform built to optimize 190/193 emergency response and incident creation through software, automation, integration, and artificial intelligence.
case.summary: A platform built to transform the initial cycle of 190 and 193 emergency response, structuring information, automating workflows, and integrating resources to make incident creation faster, more consistent, and more efficient.

productVisual.ariaLabel: Abstract visual composition of the Hefesto operational flow, from the call to dispatch

context.label: 01 / CONTEXT
context.p1: Emergency response begins long before a team reaches the scene. The call needs to be understood, the location identified, essential information organized, and the incident recorded clearly enough for the operational process to continue.
context.p2: In a high-volume environment, every step adds time. Small inefficiencies, when multiplied across thousands of calls, become a significant operational problem.

challenge.label: 02 / THE CHALLENGE
challenge.p1: The challenge was not simply to make call handling faster. It was to reduce the time required to structure an incident while preserving quality, consistency, and enough information for the teams continuing the response.
challenge.p2: The process involved multiple tasks: understanding the caller's report, identifying the correct location, recording data, structuring the narrative, and preparing the incident to continue through the operational workflow.
challenge.p3: Every step dependent on manual entry increased both operator workload and the time required to complete the record.

solution.label: 03 / THE SOLUTION
solution.p1: Hefesto was designed to organize the initial incident cycle into a single operational experience.
solution.p2: Instead of relying exclusively on manual entry, the system uses structured workflows, automation, lookups, and integrations to support the operator while the incident is being created.
solution.p3: The platform brings together context, location, call information, and supporting resources to reduce repetitive steps and transform data collected during the call into a more consistent operational record.

ai.label: 06 / AI & AUTOMATION
ai.p1: Automation and artificial intelligence are used to reduce mechanical tasks and organize information generated during emergency calls.
ai.p2: Voice processing, transcription, language models, and structured content generation can support stages such as interpretation, organization, and narrative construction.
ai.p3: The goal is not to remove control from the operator, but to allow more attention to be focused on the caller and less on repetitive data entry.

pipeline.ariaLabel: Hefesto artificial intelligence pipeline, with the operator remaining in final control
pipeline.operatorNote: The operator remains in control of the decision.

architecture.label: 07 / ARCHITECTURE
architecture.headlineLine2: to work as a single system.
architecture.p1: Hefesto integrates different technologies and services to connect telephony, information processing, databases, and operational systems used in the response workflow.
architecture.p2: The architecture was designed to allow continuous product evolution without losing the stability required in a high-demand environment.

scale.label: 08 / SCALE
scale.p1: In a high-volume operation, reducing minutes from an activity performed thousands of times becomes more than an interface improvement — it becomes an operational gain at scale.

impact.label: 09 / IMPACT
impact.p1: The result is a flow in which technology and automation take on part of the repetitive work, while the operator remains at the center of the operation.
impact.p2: The reduction in incident creation time, combined with more structured information, shows how apparently small improvements can produce significant impact when applied to a real, large-scale operation.
